We need to create a test class for the focal method numOf(Number) in CashFlow. The test should initialize necessary fields and dependencies within setup methods, handle cleanup, not invoke private methods, refer to given phase in existing test class for guidance, add imports, ensure no syntax errors.

We need to test that CashFlow.numOf delegates to BarSeries.numOf. So we can mock BarSeries and verify that numOf is called and returns appropriate Num.

We need to create a CashFlow instance. Its constructors require BarSeries and Position or TradingRecord. For testing numOf, we can use the simplest constructor: CashFlow(BarSeries barSeries, Position position). Provide a mock Position (or real). The constructor also does calculations; may need to stub methods on BarSeries used in constructor: barSeries.numOf(1) and barSeries.getEndIndex(), etc. In constructor, values = new ArrayList<>(Collections.singletonList(numOf(1))); So it calls numOf(1) on the mock BarSeries. Then calculate(position) and fillToTheEnd(barSeries.getEndIndex()). Those methods may depend on other BarSeries methods like getBarSeries, getValue, etc. To avoid complexity, we can use a spy or a subclass? But we are not allowed to invoke private methods. However we can mock BarSeries to return simple values for methods used in calculation, but calculate may rely on many methods. Simpler: Use a real BarSeries implementation like MockBarSeries from existing tests. But then we cannot verify delegation because we need to check that CashFlow.numOf calls barSeries.numOf. We could spy on BarSeries (using Mockito.spy) on a real MockBarSeries, then verify invocation.

Approach: In setupBeforeEach, create a MockBarSeries with some data, then spy it: BarSeries barSeries = spy(new MockBarSeries(numFunction, 1d,2d,3d)); However need numFunction; test class extends nothing, but we can define a NumFunction using a lambda that uses DecimalNum? The library uses Num interface; we can use org.ta4j.core.num.DecimalNum.numOf(double). But we need a Function<Number, Num>. In existing tests, they extend AbstractIndicatorTest which provides numFunction. Here we can create a simple function: number -> org.ta4j.core.num.DecimalNum.valueOf(number.doubleValue()) or use DecimalNum.numOf. Import DecimalNum.

We'll create a static Function<Number, Num> NUM_FUNCTION = n -> DecimalNum.valueOf(n.doubleValue());

Then create barSeries = spy(new MockBarSeries(NUM_FUNCTION, 1d,2d,3d));

Create a Position: new Position(); (simple).

Create CashFlow cashFlow = new CashFlow(barSeries, new Position());

Now test method: Number input = 5; Num result = cashFlow.numOf(input); Verify that barSeries.numOf(input) was called once and result equals whatever barSeries returns. We need to stub barSeries.numOf to return a specific Num, e.g., DecimalNum.valueOf(42). Use when(barSeries.numOf(input)).thenReturn(expectedNum);

But note: The constructor already called barSeries.numOf(1) during initialization, which we need to stub before constructing CashFlow. So we can set up stub for numOf(1) before constructing. Use when(barSeries.numOf(1)).thenReturn(DecimalNum.ONE); Also stub getEndIndex maybe used in fillToTheEnd. Use when(barSeries.getEndIndex()).thenReturn(2); Also stub getBarSeries? Not needed.

But calculate may call other methods like getBarSeries, getValue, etc. To avoid errors, we can use a simpler constructor that doesn't call calculate? All constructors call calculate. So mocking may be complex. Alternative: Use a subclass of CashFlow that overrides calculate to no-op for test. But we cannot modify target class. However we can create a spy of CashFlow and stub calculate after construction? But calculate is called in constructor before we can stub. Could use Mockito.mock(CashFlow.class, withSettings().useConstructor(barSeries, new Position()).defaultAnswer(CALLS_REAL_METHODS).lenient()) and then stub calculate? Not sure.

Simpler: Use the constructor that takes BarSeries and TradingRecord with finalIndex, which also calls calculate. So still.

Maybe we can avoid constructor side effects by using reflection to instantiate CashFlow without invoking constructor? Not allowed to invoke private methods but can use reflection? Might be overkill.

Alternative: Use a real BarSeries and Position; rely on actual calculation but we only care that numOf returns correct value. We can test that cashFlow.numOf returns same as barSeries.numOf for a given number, regardless of internal calculations. Use real MockBarSeries; no mocking needed. Then we don't need to verify invocation, just assert equality.

Test: Create MockBarSeries with numbers, create CashFlow with new Position. Call cashFlow.numOf(2.5) and compare to barSeries.numOf(2.5). That tests delegation.

Thus we don't need mocking. Setup: In @BeforeEach, create barSeries and cashFlow.

Also test that passing null throws NPE? Not required.

Implement test method testNumOfDelegates.

Add imports: org.ta4j.core.num.DecimalNum; java.util.function.Function; org.ta4j.core.mocks.MockBarSeries; org.ta4j.core.Position; org.ta4j.core.analysis.CashFlow; org.ta4j.core.BarSeries; org.ta4j.core.num.Num; org.junit.jupiter.api.Test; etc.

Implement.

Teardown not needed.
